subject: Hosted API pricing - token volumes & peak TPS
messages:
From: Sam Johnson <sam.johnson@acmeretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmeretail.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up - hosted API volumes and peak TPS

Hi Marissa / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo today — super helpful. As promised, here are the numbers we discussed for our initial hosted API run:

- Expected monthly token volume (starting 1Q): 180M - 240M tokens (conservative to expected).
- Primary workload: user-facing chat generation (avg ~120 tokens/generation) + some short structured prompts. Embeddings usage is negligible in month 1 (<5%).
- Peak traffic: we typically see ~200 concurrent users on promo days; that maps roughly to a peak of ~600 tokens/sec (TPS) during spikes. Average TPS across the month looks closer to 80 TPS.
- Budget band (for hosted/API costs): roughly $4k - $9k / month initially. We may expand if latency/cost tradeoffs look good.

Can you confirm next steps for an indicative hosted API price (target $/1M tokens) at these volumes, and whether we should consider a dedicated/reserved capacity conversation given the peak TPS?

I attached our rough volume forecast (acme-volume-estimates.csv).

Best,
Sam
Sam Johnson
Head of Product, Acme Retail
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sam Johnson <sam.johnson@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up - hosted API volumes and peak TPS

Hi Sam — thanks for the detailed numbers and the CSV, that’s perfect. Quick recap and a few clarifying Qs so we can put together an apples-to-apples pricing estimate: 

Recap:
- Monthly tokens: 180M-240M (we'll model both the low and expected cases).
- Avg tokens/request: ~120
- Peak TPS (tokens/sec): ~600 during spikes; ~80 avg.
- Embeddings negligible for month 1.

Clarifying questions:
1) What percentage of requests are chat generations vs short prompts vs system/batch jobs? (Even a rough split helps us size concurrency.)
2) For the peak TPS metric, is 600 TPS a short spike (<5 minutes) or sustained (tens of minutes)?
3) Any P95/P99 latency SLO expectations? E.g., P95 < 300ms token latency or similar?

Next steps from our side: I’ll run numbers for both hosted API (usage pricing) and a quick reserved capacity estimate. Attached is our standard pricing sheet for hosted API reference (redwood-pricing-sheet.xlsx). For ballpark, at ~200M tokens/month, customers typically target $/1M tokens in the $20-$40 range depending on model and tokenization mix — I’ll aim to model $25, $30, and $35 /1M scenarios so you can see unit economics.

I’ll loop Ben for reserved-capacity thoughts if the peak profile looks sustained.

If you can answer the 3 Qs above and confirm whether the CSV includes hourly breakdowns, I’ll get a first-pass estimate to you by Monday.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Sam Johnson <sam.johnson@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 16:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up - hosted API volumes and peak TPS

Sam — quick note from infra side: if that 600 TPS (tokens/sec) spike is sustained for >15 minutes and you care about tail latency, reserved capacity (Dedicated) usually makes sense — we can give much tighter P95/P99 SLAs and better unit economics for high sustained throughput.

If it’s short bursts (<5 min), our hosted API with autoscaling + KV caching often handles it well and can be materially cheaper. Either way, Marissa will share modeled $/1M scenarios.

Also — if you can share the sample hourly traffic (even a 24-hour sample), that helps us recommend batching/cache/quantization profiles.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: Sam Johnson <sam.johnson@acmeretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:10:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up - hosted API volumes and peak TPS

Thanks Marissa / Ben — quick answers below and I attached the hourly export you requested (acme-volume-estimates.csv).

1) Workload split: ~90% chat generation, ~5% short prompts (lookup-style), ~5% admin/batch jobs.
2) Peak duration: the 600 TPS spikes are typically short promo bursts, ~3-7 minutes.
3) Latency SLO: we'd like P95 generation latency < 500ms ideally, P99 < 1.5s — but open to recommendations.

Budget: tagging $6k - $9k / month as the current run rate we can approve. If the unit economics look strong we can expand.

Ask: can you send a short two-line pricing estimate for hosted API (3 scenarios: $25/$30/$35 per 1M tokens) and a note on whether reserved capacity is recommended given the short bursty peak profile? If we look good I’ll pull procurement folks in next week.

Best,
Sam
